a5115.speech: Said that many bodabodas are ridden by people without much education, because many of those who have completed degrees want office jobs ; "The kind of scholarship we produce at colleges has a problem: a young person finishes a degree and sees that doing bodaboda is out of the question; many see education as meaning working in an office, but in Kenya you will find them riding bodabodas and daladalas, and these are the ones who are in a position to make progress." ; said that if this work were done by degree holders the economy could change, because they know how to manage money and what needs to be done in order to advance.

a5115.speaker: Dr Luka Mkonongwa, lecturer at the University of Dodoma (Udom) and education stakeholder
a5115.speech: Said that besides bringing employment to young people who have finished college, the losses incurred are greater than the benefits; said bodabodas have been causing deaths and disability, something which reduces the nation's workforce that could have been used in other sectors ; "If you want to know that this matter is difficult, even its supervision is as if it is not being done as required: look at the issue of wearing helmets, who is following up? Look at those carrying two passengers ('mshikaki'), who is following up? It is as if they have decided to keep quiet. Increasing bodabodas is like increasing deaths."

a5115.speaker: Crime and Road Safety Incidents Statistics 2023 (report)
a5115.speech: According to the statistics, in the period from January to December 2023 a total of 435 motorcycle accident incidents were reported compared with 448 in the same period in 2022, 13 fewer or 2.9 per cent; however, road accident deaths rose by 44, from 332 in 2022 to 376 in 2023, an increase of 13.3 per cent.

a5115.speaker: Tanzania Police Force (report)
a5115.speech: According to the Police Force, these accidents are caused by a lack of road safety education among some motor vehicle users and by failure to follow road safety laws ; "Dilapidated vehicles, poor infrastructure, drunkenness, negligence and the presence of substandard spare parts," the Police Force report stated.

a5115.speaker: Muhimbili Orthopaedic Institute (Moi)
a5115.speech: Says it receives about 700 road accident casualties a month, of whom 60 per cent - six out of every 10 injured - result from motorcycle-related accidents, popularly known as bodaboda.

a5115.speaker: Dr Lemeri Mchome, Acting Director of the Muhimbili Orthopaedic Institute
a5115.speech: "To a large extent, most patients have a direct link to motorcycle accidents: either they were passengers, a bajaji driver, or a car was involved in an accident because it was swerving to avoid a bodaboda or bajaji." ; "The remaining 25 per cent are young people who have no relatives at all; they came to town to look for income. We stay with them for more than three months, and costs increase." ; said many of them are injured in the head, while 75 per cent are injured in the arms and legs ; "The need for equipment is for those patients who have broken backs and large bones, and that is why we are asking stakeholders to come and help them." ; said that under the Health Policy the Ministry covers their treatment, but later, when relatives come forward, they are asked to contribute to that treatment.

a5123.speaker: Dr Hussein Ali Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a5123.speech: Described the logo as 'not just a trademark, but a symbol of our national identity'; emphasised that the mark would promote pride in Tanzanian products, stimulate local industries, and serve as a beacon of authenticity and quality for global consumers ; "This mark will not only help our products compete internationally, but it will also build consumer confidence. It reflects the creativity, value and identity of our people" ; urged Tanzanians to support the initiative by prioritising locally made goods and directed both Union and Zanzibar industry ministries, alongside the Tanzania Trade Development Authority (TanTrade), to roll out awareness campaigns and educate producers on proper logo use.

a5123.speaker: Dr Selemani Jafo, Minister for Industry and Trade
a5123.speech: Noted that the timing was ideal: "Our output in several key sectors exceeds local demand. It's time to formally brand these products for international markets." ; explained that TanTrade had overseen a national competition to design the logo, with more than 80 entries submitted.

a5123.speaker: Dr Latifa Khamis, TanTrade Director General
a5123.speech: Affirmed the authority's commitment to pushing the brand to global recognition; cited Tanzania's showcase at the Osaka Expo, where the country's pavilion attracted more than 4.7 million visitors ; "We are launching a comprehensive campaign to familiarise both businesses and consumers with the new brand. This will elevate expectations around product quality and reliability."

a5123.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a5123.speech: Backed the initiative, highlighting its potential to strengthen Tanzania's competitive advantage within the East African Community (EAC) and beyond; pointed out that intra-EAC trade had grown from 2 billion US dollars in 2005 to over 6 billion US dollars by 2014, and that a visible, trusted national brand would help Tanzania stand out in this expanding market ; "Tanzania's products must be trusted, visible and easy to identify across borders. We urge producers to use all available media, including digital platforms, to promote this brand."

a5123.speaker: Sauda Kipendi, spice trader from Zanzibar
a5123.speech: Expressed optimism: "This logo gives us a professional edge. Until now, every business used its own branding. We have waited long enough and we are excited it's finally here."

a5123.speaker: Catty Wang, Executive Director of the East Africa Commercial & Logistics Centre (EACLC)
a5123.speech: Noted that foreign investors, particularly from China, are increasingly drawn to Tanzania's production ecosystem ; "Tanzanian entrepreneurs now have an opportunity to export under a nationally backed identity, which gives legitimacy and recognition to their goods."

a5123.speaker: Amir Esmail, coffee exporter and owner of Amir Hamza (T) Ltd
a5123.speech: "We already have company trademarks, but not a national brand. This logo finally fills that gap and gives our products a chance to standout."

a5123.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a5123.speech: Acknowledged challenges that could hinder the long term success of the initiative, including quality enforcement, the risk of counterfeit goods undermining the brand's credibility, producer awareness and capacity-building, and infrastructure and logistics.

a5123.speaker: Tanzania Trade Development Authority (TanTrade)
a5123.speech: Has committed to integrating branding education into its ongoing SME development programmes, and is also forming partnerships with financial institutions and regulators to support certification, packaging and compliance for producers.

a5134.speaker: Salah Ahmed Jama, Deputy Prime Minister of the Federal Government of Somalia
a5134.speech: “Regarding growth indicators, Somalia ranks among the lowest in the world. I am certain that at least 20,000 people have sought medical treatment abroad in the past three months.”

a5134.speaker: Salah Ahmed Jama, Deputy Prime Minister of the Federal Government of Somalia
a5134.speech: “Somalia's primary export is livestock, and Saudi Arabia is a major market for it. The Ministry of Commerce needs to find new markets.”

a5147.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a5147.speech: has pushed for Namibia and Tanzania to move from political freedom to economic liberation by strengthening industrialisation, value addition and intra-African trade.

a5147.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a5147.speech: has urged African countries to fully implement the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to boost trade, industrialisation and economic growth across the continent.

a5147.speaker: Lucia Witbooi, Vice President of Namibia
a5147.speech: has called on African countries to strengthen economic cooperation and reduce dependence on external markets, saying Africa must take greater control over its own development and industrialisation.

a5147.speaker: John Mutorwa, Minister of Works and Transport
a5147.speech: tabled a motion calling on the National Assembly to ratify the Revised African Maritime Transport Charter.

a5147.speaker: Participants at the 7th African Tourism Leadership Forum and Awards in Gaborone
a5147.speech: emphasized the importance of intra-African trade for the continent.

a5413.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, President of Egypt
a5413.speech: Insisted on the importance of the Egyptian-European parliamentary dialogue and described this partnership as “an essential bridge between the peoples of the two shores of the Mediterranean.”

a5413.speaker: Roberta Metsola, President of the European Parliament
a5413.speech: Praised the role of Cairo, which she described as a “fundamental pillar of stability in the Middle East and in the southern Mediterranean.”

a5413.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi and Roberta Metsola (jointly)
a5413.speech: Agreed to intensify parliamentary exchanges between Egypt and the European Union and stressed the need for a sustained political dialogue founded on regional stability and economic cooperation ; stressed the need to continue economic and security coordination between Egypt and the European Union, as a continuation of the comprehensive strategic cooperation announced in March 2024.

a5413.speaker: Roberta Metsola, President of the European Parliament
a5413.speech: Praised the Egyptian mediation that made it possible to obtain a ceasefire in the Gaza Strip, considering that this agreement “would not have been possible without the personal efforts of President Al-Sisi” ; reaffirmed, on behalf of the European Union, support for the two-State solution, in line with the Egyptian vision of a stability founded on respect for national sovereignties.

a5413.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, President of Egypt
a5413.speech: Set out his country’s initiatives to make the ceasefire durable, to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid and to prepare the international conference on the reconstruction of Gaza, scheduled for November in Cairo.

a5413.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi and Roberta Metsola (jointly)
a5413.speech: Agreed to strengthen cooperation on irregular migration through the creation of employment programmes for skilled Egyptian labour, the facilitation of student mobility and vocational training in European countries; according to both parties, these initiatives should contribute to social stability and sustainable development in the countries of origin and transit.

a5462.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
a5462.speech: Announced that Arthur Peter Mutharika is set to be officially declared winner of the September 16 presidential election, saying the final results will be released tomorrow.

a5462.speaker: Sangwani Mwafulirwa, MEC's Director of Media and Public Relations
a5462.speech: Said the commission is finalising all electoral processes and confirmed that no injunctions have been served to halt the results: "The Commission will not be able to give any update tonight, as many were anticipating. We are working on finalising all electoral processes in order to announce the final results within the appropriate time, possibly tomorrow," Mwafulirwa told journalists at the National Tally Centre, BICC in Lilongwe.

a5462.speaker: Reverend Billy Gamah, leader of the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a5462.speech: The Malawi Council of Churches has urged President Chakwera to acknowledge defeat as a demonstration of statesmanship and to help maintain peace ; "The table cannot change to deliver victory for President Chakwera. Conceding early will show maturity, promote peace, and help the nation move forward without unnecessary tension."

a5462.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former president of Malawi
a5462.speech: Has issued a similar appeal for President Chakwera to concede.

a5467.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a5467.speech: "God is a democrat, which is why democracy is non-negotiable. For us, the world can only move towards democracy in order to solve its problems." ; Holds that Benin's 25-year-old democracy is an irreversible process, all the more so as his country shares the values of the free world.

a5467.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a5467.speech: Maintains that this democracy needs to be supported by strong institutions working for the general interest: "One cannot conceive of a democracy without the rule of law, and there is no rule of law without a functioning justice system. Without justice, one cannot fight impunity and corruption. We must make progress in the area of sanctions, otherwise we will not be able to attract investors."

a5467.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a5467.speech: Said Benin defends freedom of expression through the flourishing of the media, which deserve to be reformed for a more solid democratic anchoring; also defends the freedom of the population to move about in production centres, which presupposes the need to guarantee their security by investing more in the fight against terrorism.

a5467.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a5467.speech: Welcomed the signing of the second MCA compact, given the infrastructure challenge still facing Benin: "Energy will make it possible to create economies of scale in order to promote self-employment and move towards strong growth."

a5467.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a5467.speech: Taking stock of the first MCA compact, considers that the programme genuinely brought added value to Benin's economy, particularly through improved performance of the Port of Cotonou and the modernisation of justice, financial services and land tenure; acknowledged that where Benin stumbled was in the fight against corruption, which explains the delay in obtaining eligibility for the second compact: "The MCA is a tool that responds to the economic and social transformation needs of our country. Today we are ready to correct our shortcomings in order to carry out the second-generation MCA successfully."

a5467.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a5467.speech: Considers that the first generation of MCA already includes elements of integration insofar as the investments made had a knock-on effect on the whole sub-region, and that an additional effort by the American programme towards integrating projects would be welcome.

a5467.speaker: Dana Hyde, Executive Director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a5467.speech: Argues that investment in the energy sector is today an imperative for Benin; recalls that only a third of the country's population has electricity and those who do not have it full-time: "The compact uses a comprehensive approach to develop a sustainable energy sector for Benin." ; Confides that eligibility for the MCA rests on a rigorous selection process through indicators relating to economic freedom, governance, and the country's level of investment in its people; Benin's new eligibility, following Ghana and Cape Verde, constitutes for her a performance indicator to be applauded.

a5467.speaker: Dana Hyde, Executive Director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a5467.speech: Also supports the need for African countries to invest more in integrating their economies; the MCA programme plans in this regard to put in place regional compacts in the coming years: "We are optimistic that we will be able to do it."

a5494.speaker: Mohlomi Moleko, Acting Minister of Energy and Minister of Natural Resources of Lesotho
a5494.speech: Told Public Eye that indeed Matlanyane last year signed the controversial deal with BJT on behalf of government, calling the signed document a 'financing agreement' and not a contract ; "It's a financing agreement. All such deals are signed by the Minister of Finance" ; "it's a build-transfer-operated model, meaning I can't sign such an agreement when the finance minister is around" ; "When it's a loan agreement, she (Matlanyane) will take the lead as long as it involves the government giving guarantees, but when she takes it to cabinet, she will need the concurrence of the Minister of Energy. If you were privy to cabinet minutes, you would actually see that this issue was discussed in three meetings."

a5494.speaker: Mohlomi Moleko, Acting Minister of Energy of Lesotho
a5494.speech: Curated the process of applying for a tariff, which ultimately ends with the regulator LEWA for approval ; "The LEC (Lesotho Electricity Corporation) hires a consultant, who will be paid by the World Bank, who assesses whether the tariff is acceptable; how much will the Independent Power Producers (IPP) charge; how much profit will they make over a certain period of time" ; "There's no such thing" (when asked about the consultant's advice) ; "He would be entering into a political terrain if he gave that advice. Is the rate acceptable? It's not the mandate of the consultant to indicate whether the price is right or wrong."

a5494.speaker: Mohlomi Moleko, Acting Minister of Energy of Lesotho
a5494.speech: Told Public Eye that he's thinking of suing the publication over what he deemed as "defaming" and "writing lies about the minister," a statement which he told MoAfrika FM earlier this month ; "I want to take upon myself (to sue or institute legal proceedings). You news reporters like writing lies, you need to verify your sources."

a5494.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Lesotho (press statement)
a5494.speech: Castigated this publication over its not only "incorrect but also misleading" articles ; "The Ministry wishes to inform the public that the cabinet authorized the Honourable Minister of Finance and Development Planning, Dr Retselisitsoe Matlanyane, to sign a USD 53 million Build-Operate-Transfer Financing agreement for the 40 MWp solar power plant and integrated 20 MWH energy storage system located at Ha Ramarothele in the Mafeteng district. The agreement is between the Government of Lesotho and Beijing Jingyuntong Technology Co. Limited (BJT)" ; indicates that it's "well within the Minister of Finance's powers to sign this kind of agreement in terms of the Public Financial Management and Accountability Act No 12 of 2011 and Loans and Guarantees Act No. 15 of 1967 (as Amended) and Public Private Partnership Policy of 2011."

a5494.speaker: Dr Retselisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
a5494.speech: Blocked these reporters on WhatsApp and direct calls when trying to seek her comment; before that sent an angry text noting, "Let's respect each other; if you are truly a genuine journalist, you will not ask me frivolous questions since you will not even reveal your sources (of information)... I am not interested" ; "Evening...the day you would like us to talk and respect each other at our respective workplaces, you will request a meeting in an appropriate manner. Rephrase your questions, and then we will address each other appropriately about the issues you are inquiring about."

a5494.speaker: A source with intimate knowledge of the deal (anonymous)
a5494.speech: Told this publication that Matlanyane was out of her depth and confines of the law when she signed the agreement ; "LEC enters into an IPP for negotiations on the technicalities; they agree or disagree. What is the basis of the finance minister signing a deal of which she already signed even before going to cabinet?" ; "Only after there's been an accord from the Minister of Energy can Matlanyane sign; that process was not followed. She usurped the powers of the LEC and LEWA in agreeing to the M2.20 tariff; it's fraud."

a5494.speaker: Check-Mate Lesotho (fact-checking colleagues)
a5494.speech: Found that according to the Lesotho Electricity Authority (LEA) Act of 2002, the Minister of Natural Resources bears the sole responsibility on transactions of this nature.

a5494.speaker: Lesotho Electricity Authority (LEA) Act of 2002 (statute)
a5494.speech: "Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 107, the Lesotho Electricity Corporation or its successor company is entitled to continue importing electricity from Eskom, pursuant to any agreements between Lesotho Electricity Corporation and Eskom that are in force on the commencement of this Act" ; Section 107 (103) explicitly notes that "the Authority shall, before issuing the license referred to in Subsection (1), consult the Minister (of Natural Resources) on the matter."

a5494.speaker: Motlatsi Ramafole, LEWA Chief Executive
a5494.speech: Sensationally confirmed that the regulator's board did indeed approve an exorbitant M2.20 tariff ; "Yes, we did approve the tariff on the basis of financial analysis that was presented to us," adding that they convened on December 23, 2024 ; "We (the board) were not coerced into accepting the rate; it's our job to make such analysis, especially since we sat during the week, not on a holiday" ; "Eyebrows shouldn't be raised."

a5494.speaker: Build-Operate-Transfer Agreement for the 35MW Solar Farm and 20MW Energy Storage (13-page contract document)
a5494.speech: Section 8, titled Tax and Duty Exemptions, notes: "During the construction phase, the Government of Lesotho agrees to waive all customs, duties, and value-added taxes (VAT) in respect of the importation of goods and materials necessary for the construction of the project. However, income tax is not exempt during the construction phase and shall be payable in accordance with applicable tax laws" ; Section 7, read with 7.1, 7.2, and 7.3, indicates: "The price of electricity generated by the project in the first year of operation will be set at 2.2 rand/KWh, with a 5 percent (five percent) annual increase. Payments for electricity will be settled in US (United States of America) dollars at the agreed exchange rate," and "Payments shall be made every 60 (sixty) days" ; Section 2.1 states that the BJT will manage the project for a period of 15 years, retaining the rights to all revenue generated during this time: "All revenues generated from the sale of electricity belong to BJT (Beijing Jingyuntong Technology)" ; Section 9.7 notes: "Unless otherwise agreed in writing by both parties, any such negotiation or arbitration shall be held in Johannesburg (South Africa), and the language to be used in the arbitration proceedings shall be in English..." ; Clause 13 bars the government and BJT from disclosing the contents of the deal "leading to this Agreement and the information handed over to such Party during the course of negotiations, as well as the details of all the transactions or agreements contemplated in this Agreement and any matters incidental thereto."

a5494.speaker: A source with intimate knowledge of the Ha Ramarothole project (anonymous)
a5494.speech: "They (authorities) have used an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) from Phase I, which was so bad that there's presently colossal soil erosion and land degradation in the project areas, with an estimated cost of M28 million to rehabilitate the place" ; said such incompetence is similar to the one that has led to the World Bank team landing in Maseru this week to assess the Ha Belo and Ha Tikoe substations, which have not commenced; also indicated that before being axed, former energy minister Professor Nqosa Mahao established a forensic team to investigate alleged corruption at the national utility company in energy-related deals.

a5494.speaker: Professor Nqosa Mahao, then Minister of Energy of Lesotho (before parliament's Natural Resources Portfolio Committee)
a5494.speech: Highlighted that lessons learnt from Phase I of the project included badly done Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) reports ; "Yes, these are experiences that we have had and on the issue of EIA, you can see that it was badly done on Phase I. We are going to be far off vigilant in Phase II and exercise absolute due diligence."

a5494.speaker: Mantsabeng Lifalakane, officer of the Ministry of Energy of Lesotho
a5494.speech: "There is land degradation and soil erosion at Ha Ramarothole project construction site, we are already addressing that. We started addressing it in November, but we had limited. This year we have enough funding to rehabilitate the dongas that are worrisome."

a5494.speaker: Machesetsa Mofomobe, Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a5494.speech: Said only the courts of law will nullify the 'corrupt' $350 million BJT deal ; "Government should have been honest and transparent about deal thus they issued a vague statement from Finance; the missive lacks details about the dates on which processes of approving the tariff were done" ; "LEC (Lesotho Electricity Company) should have had engagements with IPP (Independent Power Producer) and agreed on the tariff then write to LEWA (Lesotho Electricity and Water Authority) for approval," adding that at that stage public consultations should have happened; indicated that after such the LEC then informs the Minister of Energy who presents a paper to cabinet "but since this deal is corrupt" Matlanyane "signed it retrospectively even before cabinet approved" ; "The courts will nullify this deal," while urging the finance ministry to produce a timeline of events that led to the inking of the agreement.

a5494.speaker: Motlalentoa Letsosa, Democratic Congress (DC) deputy leader
a5494.speech: Echoed Mofomobe's sentiments describing the agreement as "corrupt to the core" ; "I suspect that there are people who will or have personally benefitted from this crazy deal" ; "Electricity is already expensive hence one will not be surprised when consumers find 'creative ways' to access it... Ultimately government will have bail out the utility company since customers will not be able to afford the ballooning tariff price" ; noted that the line ministry being Energy should have been at the forefront before Finance approved the deal: "Energy has the technical skills to assess the viability of such agreements then only after satisfying itself Finance will also assess whether there's value for money, but in this case procedural steps were not followed."

a5494.speaker: Mokhothu Makhalanyane, National Assembly Chairperson of Chairs
a5494.speech: Said they are concerned with such agreements which will end up being paid for by future generations ; "If such loans are inked they should be scrutinized for the value they will inject into the national economy; was there no cheaper alternative? There needs to be transparency regarding the details of that deal" ; indicated that if the deal is above board and was done within the confines of the law, there shouldn't be a resemblance of hesitation when details about the agreement are required ; "I am very unhappy with the manner in which the situation has been handled; cabinet does not own this country."

a5729.speaker: Dr Phil Mnisi, Governor of the Central Bank of Eswatini
a5729.speech: Told delegates that preparations are advanced to allow the platform, which currently settles mainly in the South African Rand, to accommodate the US Dollar and selected SADC domestic currencies: “This will enhance intra-regional trade and gradually reduce reliance on a single settlement currency”, emphasising Eswatini’s commitment to supporting financial integration within SADC.

a5729.speaker: Speakers including Adv. Magedi-Titus Thokwane and Daniel Mohau
a5729.speech: Noted that the technical infrastructure to support multiple currencies is already in place.

a5729.speaker: Officials (at the conference)
a5729.speech: Said this milestone highlighted the country’s role as a regional hub for policy dialogue and financial cooperation.

a5729.speaker: One participant (anonymous)
a5729.speech: “This is not just about payments. By hosting this conversation, Eswatini is helping to shape how the region trades.”

a5729.speaker: Delegates
a5729.speech: Stressed that while the rand will remain part of the system, adding other currencies marks a step towards monetary cooperation and economic independence within SADC.

a5915.speaker: USAID
a5915.speech: Denies directing funds to campaigns on pesticide regulations and said that its GM programme “promotes functional regulatory systems, but does not endorse regulatory decisions regarding specific products.”

a5915.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES / Lighthouse Reports investigation
a5915.speech: Reveals how the US government has been working behind the scenes to facilitate GMO crop approvals and downplay the dangers of pesticides in Nigeria, financing a public relations operation that discredited environmentalists who raised concerns about GM and pesticide risks around the world, including several prominent environmentalists in Nigeria; government documents reviewed show USAID gave the US PR firm v-Fluence more than $400,000 via a sub-contract between 2013 and 2019, and USAID granted the NBMA over $200,000 from 2016 to 2019.

a5915.speaker: Environmentalists and scientists
a5915.speech: Say that most GM crops have been designed for use alongside herbicides, most commonly glyphosate, the weedkiller first patented by Monsanto.

a5915.speaker: World Health Organisation
a5915.speech: In 2015 classified glyphosate as a probable human carcinogen.

a5915.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES investigation (2022)
a5915.speech: Revealed that while many farmers were enthusiastic about being part of GM trials, many had little knowledge of what the crops were and the environmental risks associated with their use.

a5915.speaker: Bonus Eventus network profile (v-Fluence)
a5915.speech: Alleges that an organisation Mr Bassey co-founded had accused him of “engaging in fraud and misrepresentation” and that he was “found guilty by a Nigerian court and ordered to stop representing himself as affiliated with the NGO,” Friends of the Earth Nigeria; also says he “collaborated with and promoted the works of those trained in the former Soviet Union”; states that Mr Rhodes-Vivour “claims to be an MIT architecture school graduate; however, MIT continues to list him as a graduate student without having conveyed a specific degree”, and alleges he made “false and unsubstantiated claims about genetically modified foods”; criticises Charles Anudu as “supporting anti-GMO movements to sustain existing crop chemicals” while noting the claim is “rumoured, unconfirmed.”

a5915.speaker: Nnimmo Bassey, director of Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF)
a5915.speech: Described the allegations in his profile as “misinformation”, clarifying that the 2020 lawsuit lodged against him was dismissed by the court as baseless, and described the Soviet Union allegation as “laughable”, saying “The chemical industry would always be happy to package falsehood to find favour – this is absolutely ridiculous.”

a5915.speaker: Nnimmo Bassey, director of Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF)
a5915.speech: “To me, what is disturbing is that the governments, which should protect the lives of people, would invest in people who do hatchet jobs and try to use that to expose Nigerians to the risks of GMOs. I’m surprised that the US government would pay attention to such false information.”

a5915.speaker: Jay Byrne, head of v-Fluence
a5915.speech: Denied any past or current contracts with the US government but said that the US government does fund “other organisations with whom we work”; wrote in a statement to Lighthouse Reports: “We’ve had multiple projects funded by the US and other governments.” ; Asserted in a written statement to Lighthouse Reports that his profiles only use “publicly available and referenced information” ; Denied allegations in the US lawsuit over paraquat, saying they are based on claims which are “manufactured and false.”

a5915.speaker: National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA) (email response)
a5915.speech: Said it acts are “void of external influence in its decisions and determinations”, while acknowledging that it worked with “international agencies that align with our statutory mandate” on the 2015 NBMA Act “in the areas of knowledge sharing” and for the speedy realisation of the Agency’s mandate; wrote that the agency is part of the sovereign government and operates without “external influence”, that some staff received a v-Fluence newsletter only “to be in tune with global happenings in the sector”, and added: “The NBMA wishes to also state categorically that it has no affiliation with v-fluence or Jay Byrne.”

a5915.speaker: USAID spokesperson
a5915.speech: Said that its GM programme “provides technical and capacity development support to partner-country biosafety regulatory agencies who seek to develop robust, functional regulatory systems to oversee use of agricultural biotechnologies.”

a5915.speaker: Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, Labour Party 2023 Lagos State governorship candidate
a5915.speech: Described the profiling as “a tactic, a strategy” which the agrochemical industry uses as a “way of diverting people’s attention from the actual issues raised about their products”; raised concerns about the “toxication of the environment” and the “effect of human health” brought on by pesticides and GMOs, and expressed frustration that governments and industry are spending resources “attacking” the people warning of these harms rather than working to mitigate them.

a5915.speaker: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
a5915.speech: Has publicly verified that Mr Rhodes-Vivour indeed obtained a master’s degree from its architecture school.

a5915.speaker: Abdallah el-Kurebe, agricultural journalist
a5915.speech: Confirmed that he registered with Bonus Eventus on 14 April 2014, but said he has “not utilised their services or participated in any of their activities”; wrote: “While my articles may have been referenced by others, this does not imply my endorsement or involvement with those entities.”

a5915.speaker: Agnes Asagbra, Director General/CEO of the National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA)
a5915.speech: Said she was recommended by her immediate predecessor, Rufus Ebegba, to sign up to Bonus Eventus as a way “to gather as much information as I could to help me in the execution of my work as the DG of the NBMA”, and that her subscription to the newsletter was a way “to acquaint my knowledge of recent happenings in the modern biotechnology sector”, arguing it has “in no way influenced my decisions or actions”; she said she had never been to the Bonus Eventus website.

a5915.speaker: Agnes Asagbra, Director General/CEO of the National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA)
a5915.speech: Condemned v-Fluence’s profiling activities: “I would categorically say it is wrong”, describing the profiling as “unthinkable” and “unethical”; on the NBMA’s relationship with USAID she said, “This situation has shown us that the agency has to be more circumspect in its associations with other organisations going forward.”

a5915.speaker: Kazeem Oyinwola, Abuja-based lawyer at Amofin Solicitors
a5915.speech: Said the Bonus Eventus files may breach Nigerian privacy laws: “The NBMA’s collaboration with a network to profile Nigerians who are critical of GMOs and hazardous pesticides raises significant legal concerns under Nigerian law”, citing the Nigerian Data Protection Act and the Constitution; argued profiling may violate section 37 of the constitution and sections 21 to 34 of the NDPA 2023, and that “Profiling without consent also infringes on the rights of the individuals (Data Subjects) concerned as enshrined in sections 34-38 of the NDPA, and may lead to substantial penalties for the agency” ; Argued section 39 safeguards freedom of expression: “Actions by the NBMA that could suppress or disparage these expressions may infringe upon these constitutional rights. As a regulatory body, the NBMA is obligated to maintain objectivity and should not act as an advocacy group”, and said the agency may be exposed to legal challenges for overstepping its statutory mandate.

a6097.speaker: Indian military sources
a6097.speech: According to Indian military sources, Pakistani forces had violated the ceasefire by firing projectiles at Indian army posts in the Poonch region of Kashmir. In response, India reinforced its military presence and retaliated with bombardments.

a6097.speaker: Authorities on both sides (India and Pakistan)
a6097.speech: Authorities on both sides confirm casualties, including soldiers and civilians.

a6097.speaker: The Red Cross and other humanitarian organisations
a6097.speech: have already expressed concern about the safety of populations in the border areas, where dozens of families are abandoning their homes.

a6097.speaker: The international community, including the United Nations and countries such as the United States and China
a6097.speech: called for restraint on both sides and for the resumption of dialogue.

a6350.speaker: Officials in Ethiopia's Tigray region
a6350.speech: Have warned that longtime foes Ethiopia and Eritrea could be headed towards war, risking another humanitarian disaster in the Horn of Africa.

a6350.speaker: Analysts
a6350.speech: Said direct clashes between two of Africa's largest armies would signal the death blow for a historic rapprochement for which Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019 and could draw in other regional powers.

a6350.speaker: General Tsadkan Gebretensae, a vice president in the interim administration in Ethiopia's Tigray region
a6350.speech: “At any moment war between Ethiopia and Eritrea could break out,” he wrote in Africa-focused magazine the Africa Report on Monday; Tsadkan accused the dissident TPLF faction of seeking an alliance with Eritrea.

a6350.speaker: Getachew Reda, head of Tigray's interim administration
a6350.speech: Asked the government for support against the dissidents. “There is clear antagonism between Ethiopia and Eritrea,” Getachew told a news conference on Monday. “What concerns me is that the Tigray people may once again become victims of a war they don't believe in.”

a6350.speaker: Ethiopia's federal government
a6350.speech: Has not commented on the tensions.

a6350.speaker: Human Rights Concern – Eritrea (UK-based)
a6350.speech: According to UK-based Human Rights Concern – Eritrea, Eritrea ordered a nationwide military mobilisation in mid-February.

a6350.speaker: Two diplomatic sources and two Tigrayan officials (anonymous)
a6350.speech: Told Reuters that Ethiopia deployed troops toward the Eritrean border this month, asking not to be named due to the sensitivity of the situation.

a6350.speaker: Eritrean and Ethiopian government spokespeople
a6350.speech: Did not respond to requests for comment.

a6350.speaker: Payton Knopf and Alexander Rondos, former U.S. and EU envoys to the region
a6350.speech: Say the prospects of a new war are real. “The deterioration of the political and security situation in Tigray is dry tinder waiting for a match,” they wrote in an essay for U.S. publication Foreign Policy on Wednesday.

a6350.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6350.speech: Has made repeated public declarations since 2023 that landlocked Ethiopia has a right to sea access, comments some analysts view as an implicit threat of military action against Eritrea, which lies on the Red Sea.

a6367.speaker: Pete Hegseth, US Defense Secretary
a6367.speech: Hegseth told almost 50 of Ukraine’s Western backers on Wednesday that he had joined their meeting “to directly and unambiguously express that stark strategic realities prevent the United States of America from being primarily focused on the security of Europe.” ; “The United States faces consequential threats to our homeland. We must and we are focusing on security of our own borders,” he said.

a6367.speaker: Pete Hegseth, US Defense Secretary
a6367.speech: Reading the riot act to U.S. allies, Hegseth said that Ukraine will not get all its territory back from Russia and will not be allowed to join NATO, which would provide the ultimate security guarantee to ensure that Russian President Vladimir Putin never attacks it again. ; This week, Hegseth took Ukraine’s candidacy off the table.

a6367.speaker: Pete Hegseth, US Defense Secretary
a6367.speech: He insisted NATO will not be involved in any future force that might be required to police the peace in Ukraine. European and other nations will, but the Europeans will have to pay for it. No American troops would take part in such an operation, he warned. ; Beyond that, Hegseth said that NATO will not come to the rescue of any European nation involved in that force if it is attacked by Russia.

a6367.speaker: Pete Hegseth, US Defense Secretary
a6367.speech: Hegseth has now raised doubts about the U.S. commitment to that pledge [Article 5], although he did say that his country is not planning to leave the alliance.

a6367.speaker: Sébastien Lecornu, French Defense Minister
a6367.speech: said that NATO faces “a real moment of truth.” “To say that it’s the biggest and most robust alliance in history is true, historically speaking. But the real question is will that still be the case in 10 or 15 years,” he said.

a6418.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6418.speech: When he regained the American presidency a few months ago, he "announced some radical measures aimed at making America great again."

a6418.speaker: Other donors, including the United Kingdom
a6418.speech: Have also warned that aid will no longer be a priority.

a6418.speaker: United States government
a6418.speech: Only last week, the US announced a sudden termination of funding from the Millennium Challenge Corporation.

a6418.speaker: The Trump administration
a6418.speech: Has made it clear that it views us [Malawi] as careless and irresponsible.

a6418.speaker: US Embassy in Malawi (statements)
a6418.speech: Statements on the denial of American visas to so-called "Malawian diplomats", which show that Malawi's systems are so porous that even its approach to diplomacy cannot be trusted.

a6668.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Somali Prime Minister
a6668.speech: Following the Eid al-Fitr prayer, exchanged greetings with worshippers and delivered remarks honoring their sacrifices during the fasting month.

a6668.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Somali Prime Minister
a6668.speech: Addressing the congregation, called on the residents of Lower Shabelle to unite in the national campaign against Al-Shabaab: "We must all join together in the fight against Al-Shabaab. As you can see, operations are ongoing in many parts of the country."

a6812.speaker: George Mwanza, Chipata Mayor
a6812.speech: has raised concerns with foreign firms using locals to access businesses and services, as he warns that the municipality will this year not issue trading licences to businesses that are not registered with the Patents and Companies Registration Agency (PACRA). Mr Mwanza expressed concern with foreign firms using locals to access businesses and services when a delegation from PACRA, Open Ownership and USAID’s Zambia Accelerating Transparency and Integrity (ZATI), paid a courtesy call on him at his office.

a7074.speaker: European Union (EU)
a7074.speech: Announced, as the source of the report, that in response to the severe floods that continue to affect several regions of Mali it has again released 150,000 euros (more than 98 million FCFA) in humanitarian funds to meet the most urgent needs, in addition to the 1 million euros already allocated to the country under the 5.4 million euros of EU support for populations affected by devastating floods in Chad, Niger, Nigeria, Cameroon, Mali and Burkina Faso; the funding will help the Malian Red Cross respond to immediate needs for food, shelter, hygiene and logistical support and forms part of the EU's contribution to the IFRC's Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF).

a7154.speaker: Dr Oumar Totia Barry, academic and civil society actor
a7154.speech: “This decision by the Trump Administration is part of a change of ideology compared with the previous Administration. The Democrats are generally more oriented towards human rights issues and invest heavily in international public development aid, of which USAID is the main instrument. Conversely, the Republican Party gives priority to the internal priorities of the United States.” ; “The United States, like other great powers, is going through difficulties linked to pandemics, to climate and migration challenges, not to mention the trade war with China” ; “USAID represents around 64 billion dollars a year in development aid. A windfall that he wishes to put back into circulation in order to finance other socio-economic sectors that can positively affect the lives of millions of Americans.”

a7154.speaker: Dr Oumar Totia Barry, academic and civil society actor
a7154.speech: “It is a means of pressure that Trump uses against his adversaries, while seeking to establish his influence.” ; “In any case, public development aid remains an essential lever for the United States. By suspending this funding, he sends a strong message to the beneficiary countries, including Guinea,” he insists.

a7154.speaker: Dr Oumar Totia Barry, academic and civil society actor
a7154.speech: “Trump is a shrewd strategist. He often begins by sending a strong signal before renegotiating. He does not want to turn the whole world against him. USAID could be restored, perhaps with a reduced budget,” he predicts.

a7154.speaker: Dr Oumar Totia Barry, academic and civil society actor
a7154.speech: “It is a considerable shortfall,” he underlines of the loss of funding for Guinean civil society organisations, acknowledging that Trump has gone further than had been imagined in his “America First” policy, and asserting that USAID had a major impact in Guinea and elsewhere before the halt decided by the Trump Administration.

a7154.speaker: Ousmane Gaoual Diallo, Minister and government spokesperson of Guinea
a7154.speech: “It is a measure that everyone deplores, just like their withdrawal from the World Health Organization (WHO). But it also shows that America is turning towards itself, putting forward the internal concerns of Americans” ; “it is a reminder that we must take responsibility and organise ourselves so that Guineans rely first of all on themselves.”

a7154.speaker: Ousmane Gaoual Diallo, Minister and government spokesperson of Guinea
a7154.speech: “We are going to assess the impact of this decision on our functioning and our partnerships. Palliative measures will be put in place to limit its effects on our development and our populations.”

a7154.speaker: Ousmane Gaoual Diallo, Minister and government spokesperson of Guinea
a7154.speech: “The American government is fully engaged in the Simandou project, with American companies such as Wabtec, which will supply the locomotives. The financial involvement of the United States in this project far exceeds USAID's aid.”

a7154.speaker: Official of the Guinean Administration (anonymous)
a7154.speech: “Trump's decision has no impact on the ongoing demographic and health survey. The survey is continuing in accordance with the established timetable. Moreover, the part covered by USAID is already completed. What remains to be done is financed by another partner.”

a7182.speaker: Puntland civil servants
a7182.speech: warning that prolonged salary delays are paralyzing state institutions and eroding public trust in the administration's financial management.

a7182.speaker: Several Puntland government workers (anonymous)
a7182.speech: told Hiiraan Online they received just one paycheck in 2025 - for February, which was paid in March - leaving them without salaries for at least four months this year.

a7182.speaker: Mohamed Farah, Puntland State Finance Minister
a7182.speech: appeared before Puntland's parliament last month, blaming the crisis on a drop in external funding. He cited reductions in the World Bank's annual budgetary support to Puntland, a key source of financing for the region's civil service.

a7182.speaker: Puntland civil servants
a7182.speech: are urging authorities to urgently resolve the crisis, warning that continued delays could further weaken the region's already strained institutions.

a7334.speaker: Joe Manchin, US Senator
a7334.speech: "We shouldn't accept mediocrity as the best a politician can do."

a7334.speaker: Femi Adesina, former presidential spokesperson to President Muhammadu Buhari
a7334.speech: Wrote on how his principal was a compassionate president and how he cared for the poor; wrote that former President Buhari directed that because of the challenges of the pandemic and revenues that were bound to ebb, the payment of salaries must not fail – "that was the vintage Muhammadu Buhari, always thinking of the poor and underprivileged" – and that on that basis he should be called "Ore mekunu" (friend of the poor) in Yoruba language. ; Wrote about "The Big Elephant in the room. Removal of fuel subsidy": "Did you think the government didn't know that the money guzzling monster had to be slain? It knew. But who ensured that subsidies remained as long as it did? Buhari. And why? The people, the ordinary people"; acknowledged that although the civil service was over bloated, the President would not heed advice on streamlining it because he at least wanted to be remembered as someone who was paying salaries.

a7334.speaker: Sustainable Development Goals
a7334.speech: Advocate that we halve poverty by 2030.

a7450.speaker: Xi Jinping, China's President
a7450.speech: Told Modi that China and India should be partners, not rivals ; said that "both sides need to approach and handle our relationship from a strategic height and long-term perspective" and that "it is the right choice for both sides to be friends".

a7450.speaker: Narendra Modi, Indian Prime Minister
a7450.speech: Said there was now an "atmosphere of peace and stability" between them.

a7450.speaker: Narendra Modi, Indian Prime Minister
a7450.speech: Announced that flights between India and China - suspended since deadly troop clashes on their shared Himalayan border in 2020 - would resume, without providing a timeline.

a7450.speaker: Police (Tianjin)
a7450.speech: Have advised Tianjin's more than 13 million residents to avoid moving around the city if possible and to stick to shops nearby them to purchase any immediate necessities.

a7463.speaker: Statement signed by Nneamaka Okafor, media aide to the Minister of State for Petroleum, Heineken Lokpobiri
a7463.speech: According to the statement, the appointment of Adeyemi-Bero by OPEC "would provide a vital platform for Nigeria to advocate for balanced energy policies that benefit oil producers, consumers, and the global economy" ; "His appointment was confirmed at the 189th meeting of the OPEC Conference." ; "Prior to his appointment as the Chairman of the OPEC Board of Governors, he was confirmed as Nigeria's OPEC Governor for the year 2025."

a7463.speaker: Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, Nigeria's Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil)
a7463.speech: Hailed Mr. Adeyemi-Bero's elevation as a testament to the country's active contributions to the global oil industry; emphasized that this appointment provides Nigeria with a vital platform to advocate for balanced energy policies that benefit oil producers, consumers, and the global economy; also expressed profound gratitude to Ambassador Gabriel Aduda, the outgoing Nigerian OPEC Governor, for his exemplary service, acknowledging Ambassador Aduda's instrumental role in advancing Nigeria's interests within OPEC and ensuring the country's influential presence in global energy discussions.

a7463.speaker: OPEC (Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries)
a7463.speech: Has confirmed Mr. Ademola Adeyemi-Bero, Nigeria's Governor for OPEC, as Chairman of the OPEC Board of Governors for 2025; also appointed His Excellency Eng. Adeeb Al-Aama, Governor of Saudi Arabia for OPEC, as the Alternate Chairman of the Board of Governors for 2025; the OPEC Conference extended the tenure of His Excellency Haitham Al Ghais as OPEC Secretary General for another three years, effective August 1, 2025.
